title: Problem Details (RFC 7807) and Results.Problem
hook: Problem Details is the standard JSON format for HTTP API errors defined by RFC 7807. ASP.NET Core ships ProblemDetails, ValidationProblemDetails, and Results.Problem so every 4xx and 5xx response shares the same predictable shape.

blocks.text: RFC 7807 (Problem Details for HTTP Application Programming Interfaces (APIs)) defines a media type application/problem+json with core fields: type (URI identifying the problem), title (short human summary), status (HTTP status code), detail (specific explanation), and instance (URI for this occurrence). ASP.NET Core provides Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ProblemDetails and ValidationProblemDetails (adds an errors dictionary for field validation). Minimal APIs use Results.Problem(...) and Results.ValidationProblem(...). AddProblemDetails() registers customization via IProblemDetailsService and IProblemDetailsWriter for consistent production error bodies.

entries.plainDefinition: IETF standard defining application/problem+json error document structure for HTTP APIs.
ASP.NET Core model for RFC 7807 with Type, Title, Status, Detail, Instance, Extensions.
ProblemDetails subclass with Errors dictionary mapping field names to message arrays.
.NET 7+ service that writes ProblemDetails to the response with customization hooks.

blocks.text: Clients, API gateways, and mobile apps parse one error contract across all endpoints. Custom ad-hoc shapes like { error: true, msg: "..." } break gateway routing and client SDKs. Problem Details extensions carry correlationId, traceId, error codes, and retry hints without polluting top-level fields. Senior interviews contrast Problem Details vs custom errors — when extensions are enough versus when a completely custom envelope is justified.

blocks.title: Problem Details vs custom errors
blocks.body: Prefer RFC 7807 with extensions for domain codes (extensions.code = "ORDER_NOT_FOUND"). Custom top-level wrappers duplicate what extensions provide and break standards-aware clients. Only wrap if a legacy client cannot migrate.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

blocks.title: Producing Problem Details in ASP.NET Core

items.title: Return from handler or filter
items.body: Results.Problem, ValidationProblemDetails, or BadRequestObjectResult with ProblemDetails.

items.title: IProblemDetailsService serializes
items.body: Sets Content-Type application/problem+json and writes JSON including extensions.

items.title: Global handler uses same shape
items.body: IExceptionHandler calls TryWriteAsync for unhandled 500 errors with correlationId extension.

snippet.label: Results.Problem in minimal APIs
snippet.explanation: type URI identifies problem kind for clients and docs. extensions add machine-readable orderId without breaking RFC shape.

snippet.label: ValidationProblemDetails from ModelState
snippet.explanation: ValidationProblem helper returns 400 with errors dictionary — same shape as automatic [ApiController] invalid model response.

snippet.label: Global customization with correlation ID
snippet.explanation: CustomizeProblemDetails runs for all Problem Details writes — validation, Results.Problem, and IExceptionHandler. correlationId links client error to logs.

snippet.label: Problem Details vs ad-hoc custom error (avoid)
snippet.explanation: extensions.code gives domain identity inside standard format. Custom wrapper forces every client to branch on two error schemas.

blocks.title: Error response standards
rows: No single standard; often custom { message, code }

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Returning exception.StackTrace in Detail in production. Mixing Problem Details endpoints with legacy { error: string } on other routes — clients need one parser. Forgetting AddProblemDetails before IExceptionHandler — TryWriteAsync fails silently or returns empty body. Using generic type URI for every error — type should identify problem category for client branching.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: Application Insights queries on customDimensions where contentType != application/problem+json on 4xx/5xx reveals inconsistent handlers. Alert when 500 responses lack correlationId extension — indicates CustomizeProblemDetails bypass. Problem Details vs custom errors: use extensions for tenantId, errorCode, retryAfter; reserve fully custom JSON for backward-compatible BFF layers only. IProblemDetailsWriter allows multiple writers (logging + response). For Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) 422 Unprocessable Entity, some teams use status 422 with ValidationProblemDetails when distinguishing semantic validation from malformed JSON 400.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Standard; gateway friendly; one client parser
Breaks OpenAPI tooling; two schemas forever
Flat errors map — nested objects need custom keys

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying Problem Details is just ASP.NET-specific — it is RFC 7807. Returning different JSON shapes per controller. Unable to explain correlationId in extensions vs Instance field. Claiming custom errors are always better for 'flexibility' without mentioning extensions.

interviewTakeaways: Problem Details (RFC 7807) standardizes API errors with type, title, status, detail, instance, and extensions.
When not to use pure custom shape: greenfield APIs — extensions carry domain codes inside RFC 7807.
Production tip: CustomizeProblemDetails adds correlationId from X-Correlation-ID or TraceIdentifier; strip Detail on 500.

60s: RFC 7807 application/problem+json. ValidationProblemDetails adds errors map. AddProblemDetails customizes globally. Results.Problem for minimal APIs. extensions for codes — avoid parallel custom envelope.
Follow-up: how do you map domain exceptions to Problem Details type URIs?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'we return { message: ex.Message } for errors' gets you rejected — no standard, leaks internals, no correlationId.
Different error JSON per team in one API — clients and API gateways cannot unify retry/idempotency logic.

Strong answer: 'RFC 7807 everywhere. ValidationProblemDetails for 400 field errors. CustomizeProblemDetails sets correlationId extension. Domain codes in extensions.code. IExceptionHandler uses IProblemDetailsService for 500.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: OpenAPI 3.1 references problem+json. NestJS HttpException can serialize to similar shape when configured; ASP.NET Core is first-class. TypeScript clients should type ProblemDetails interface with index signature for extensions.
Fastify errors include statusCode and message; @fastify/rfc7807 plugin adds RFC 7807 serialization. ASP.NET AddProblemDetails is built-in without plugins.
